title: Set 114

sentences.ko: 이제 내가 길들여진 거지. 침대 옆 탁자에서 뭘 떨어뜨리면 내가 일어난다는 걸 알아챘거든. 그래서 이제 매일 아침 5시 30분이야. 내가 밥 주면 얘는 바로 다시 자고, 하루를 시작하는 건 나야. 그냥 누워서 무시해야지 하고 말은 계속 하는데, 거기에 물컵을 올려놨단 말이야.
sentences.text: She's got me trained at this point. She figured out that if she knocks something off the nightstand I'll get up, so now it's five thirty every single morning, and then I feed her and she goes right back to sleep and I'm the one who's up for the day. I keep saying I'm going to just lie there and ignore it, but I've got a glass of water on there.

alts.text: At this point I'm the one getting trained, not her. She figured out that if she shoves something off the nightstand I'm gonna get up, so now it's five thirty every single morning, and then I feed her and she's right back asleep and I'm up for the day. I keep saying I'm just gonna lie there and ignore it, but I've got a glass of water sitting up there.

She has me trained at this point. She has worked out that if she knocks something off the nightstand I will get up, so it is now five thirty every single morning, and then I feed her and she goes straight back to sleep while I am the one who is up for the day. I keep saying that I will simply lie there and ignore it, but I do have a glass of water on that table.

sentences.note: **She's got me trained** 는 얘가 나를 길들여 놨다는 뜻으로, 사람이 아니라 동물이 주도권을 쥔 상황을 웃으며 말할 때 씁니다. **goes right back to sleep** 는 바로 다시 잠든다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 가방도 차에 실어 놓고 준비는 다 했는데, 가 보니까 주차장이 꽉 차서 빈자리가 도로 쪽 저 끝에밖에 없더라. 거기 앉아서 그냥 대고 걸어갈까 생각했는데, 그러면 수업이 벌써 시작했을 거고 나는 늦게 들어가는 걸 진짜 싫어하거든. 그래서 그냥 차 돌려서 집에 왔어. 이게 제대로 된 이유가 아닌 건 나도 아는데, 어쨌든 그렇게 했어.
sentences.text: I had my bag in the car and everything, but I got there and the lot was completely full, and the only spot was way out by the road. So I'm sitting there thinking I could park and walk over, but by then the class would've already started, and I hate walking in late. So I just turned around and came home. And I know that's not a real reason, but that's what I did.

alts.text: My bag was in the car, I was all set, but I pull in and the lot's totally packed, and the only spot was way out by the road. So I'm sitting there thinking I could park and walk over, but the class would've started by then, and I hate walking in late. So I just turned around and went home. And yeah, I know that's not a real reason, but that's what I did.

I had my bag in the car and I was entirely prepared, but when I arrived the lot was completely full, and the only available space was far out by the road. I sat there considering that I could park and walk over, but by then the class would already have begun, and I dislike arriving late. So I turned around and drove home. I am aware that is not a real reason, but that is what I did.

sentences.note: **way out by the road** 의 way 는 거리를 강조하는 말로, 저 멀리 도로 쪽 끝이라는 뜻입니다. **walking in late** 는 시작한 뒤에 늦게 들어가는 것을 가리킵니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 자, 진짜 어이없는 부분은 여기야. 3킬로쯤 빠져서 바지를 사러 갔거든. 근데 진짜 그 바지 산 게 원인인 것 같아. 그게 3주 전인데 벌써 꽉 껴. 딱히 전과 다르게 하는 것도 없는 것 같은데, 뭔가 있긴 있나 봐. 살이 저절로 도로 찌지는 않잖아.
sentences.text: Okay, here's the part that gets me. I was down about seven pounds, so I went and bought pants, and I swear buying the pants is what did it, because that was three weeks ago and they're already tight on me. I don't feel like I've been doing anything different. But I must be, because you don't gain it back by accident.

alts.text: Okay, this is the part that kills me. I was down like seven pounds, so I went and bought pants, and I swear the pants are what did it, because that was three weeks ago and they're already tight on me. I don't feel like I'm doing anything different. But I've gotta be, because you don't gain it back by accident.

Here is the part I find most frustrating. I was down about seven pounds, so I went and purchased a pair of pants, and I am convinced that buying them is what caused it, because that was three weeks ago and they are already tight on me. I do not feel that I have been doing anything differently. But I must be, because one does not regain it by accident.

sentences.note: **here's the part that gets me** 는 제일 어이없고 속상한 대목이 여기라고 짚는 말입니다. **I was down about seven pounds** 처럼 down 뒤에 무게를 붙이면 그만큼 빠졌다는 뜻이 됩니다.

sentences.ko: 네가 계속 얘기하던 그 집에 드디어 갔어. 갈비는 네 말이 맞더라, 네가 말한 만큼 맛있었어. 그런데 토요일에는 원래 항상 밴드가 들어와? 스피커에서 한 1미터쯤 떨어진 자리에 앉았는데, 나랑 아내는 10분쯤 지나서 얘기하는 걸 포기했어. 그냥 먹으면서 서로 고개만 끄덕였어. 앞쪽에 앉혀 달라고 할 걸 그랬나?
sentences.text: So we finally went to that place you keep telling me about, and you were right about the short ribs, they were as good as you said. But do they always have a band in there on Saturdays? Because we were sitting maybe four feet from the speaker and my wife and I gave up talking about ten minutes in. We just ate and nodded at each other. Should I have asked to sit up front?

alts.text: We finally hit that place you're always telling me about, and you were right about the short ribs, they were as good as you said. But is there always a band in there on Saturdays? We were like four feet from the speaker and my wife and I gave up on talking about ten minutes in. We just ate and nodded at each other. Should I have asked to sit up front?

We finally visited the restaurant you have been recommending to me, and you were correct about the short ribs, they were as good as you said. However, do they always have a band there on Saturdays? We were seated perhaps four feet from the speaker, and my wife and I stopped trying to talk about ten minutes in. We simply ate and nodded at one another. Should I have asked to be seated up front?

sentences.note: **as good as you said** 는 네가 말한 만큼 괜찮았다고 맞장구치는 말입니다. **Should I have asked** 는 그때 부탁할 걸 그랬나 하고 지나간 일을 아쉬워하는 말투입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 솔직히? 색은 너한테 진짜 잘 어울려. 물리라는 말은 아니야. 근데 어깨가 좀 이상하게 떠 있고, 여기 서 있는 내내 네가 계속 잡아당기고 있었잖아. 그거 입을 때마다 계속 신경 쓰일걸. 누가 줄여 줄 수 있어? 아니면 원래 그렇게 나온 옷이야?
sentences.text: Honestly? The color's great on you, and I'm not telling you to take it back or anything, but it's sitting funny in the shoulders and you've been pulling at it the whole time we've been standing here. That's going to bother you every time you put it on. Can somebody take it in for you, or is that just how it's cut?

alts.text: Want the truth? The color's amazing on you, and I'm not saying take it back or anything, but it's sitting weird in the shoulders and you've been tugging at it the whole time we've been standing here. That's gonna bug you every time you put it on. Can somebody take it in for you, or is that just how it's cut?

May I be honest? The color is excellent on you, and I am not suggesting that you return it, but it is sitting oddly in the shoulders and you have been pulling at it the entire time we have been standing here. That will bother you every time you put it on. Could someone take it in for you, or is that simply how it is cut?

sentences.note: **take it in** 은 옷을 몸에 맞게 줄인다는 뜻입니다. **sitting funny** 는 옷이 몸에 이상하게 걸쳐져 맞지 않는다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 산 옷 어떠냐고 물었을 때 솔직하게 말하기

reviewed: 문장 1 캐주얼의 "I'm the one who's trained" 는 "훈련받은/숙련된 사람" 으로도 읽혀서, 누가 누구를 길들였는지 헷갈리지 않는 말로 바꿨습니다.
문장 3 격식체의 trousers 는 영국식이라 text 의 pants 와 어긋나서 pants 로 맞췄습니다.
문장 3 격식체의 "the part that troubles me" 는 text 의 "gets me"(어이없고 속상한 대목) 보다 뜻이 약해서 frustrating 으로 맞췄습니다.
문장 5 캐주얼이 text 와 첫머리가 사실상 같아서(honestly + The color's great on you) 더 구어다운 말머리로 바꿨습니다.
